newsitem.title: KENYA: E.African markets chiefs want policies harmonised.
newsitem.headline: E.African markets chiefs want policies harmonised.

text.p: Capital markets heads from Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania on Thursday called for a common strategy to mobilise regional and international savings for the economic development of one of the world's poorest regions.

At a meeting in Kenya's capital of Nairobi, they said they wanted development, harmonisation and implementation of appropriate regulatory structures and economic reforms to facilitate broad-based participation in capital markets.
The capital markets heads made their comments in a joint communique after the Nairobi meeting. They were Leo Kibirango of Uganda, Fratern Mboya of Tanzania and Kenya's Paul Melly.
Kenya, the region's economic engine, has a stock exchange capitalised at $1.89 billion. Tanzania and Uganda have pledged to have operational stock exchanges sometime in December.
The three countries are listed by the World Bank as among the 30 poorest countries of the world but have launched reforms to try to lift their economies and standards of living.

They called for the development and strengthening of stock exchanges in the region and added they had plans for a regional exchange. They wanted encouragement of cross-border listings and equal treatment of national investors of member states.

They also called for: "Protection of investors through establishment of appropriate surveillance and enforcement of established rules and regulations; general principles of accounting and auditing; full and fair disclosure of capital."

The communique said they agreed on: "Development of a regional investor compensation fund to the maximum possible extent and promotion of capital markets as a means of carrying out privatisations of state-owned companies."

The capital markets chiefs agreed on promotion and development of capital markets instruments, common professional standards among players and mutual assistance and exchange of information and training within the regional players.

They also spoke of the development of measures to stimulate capital markets, rationalise and remove barriers that unduly impeded cross-border investments and harmonisation of policies that have an impact on capital markets.

They agreed on "development and promotion of a common trading system based on the principle of enhanced transparency and efficient clearing and settlement for all capital markets transactions, including use of central depository facilities."
A central depository system is an electronic trading device that ensures immediate settlement once a bourse deal is struck.

The comunique said the capital markets chiefs had created a committee to study harmonisation of policy on cross-border listing and offerings, strategy to attract foreign portfolio investors and taxation treatment on stock exchange deals.
Other areas of to be considered for harmonisation were a wide range of capital markets laws, including rules on collective investments, loans, derivatives and pension schemes.
The committee would also examine listing and licensing requirements, trading rules, clearing and settlement and full disclosure requirements on the primary and secondary markets.
The committee will discuss enforcement of issues agreed on and the possible punishment for offenders.
